units: metres; glTF Y up, characters face +Z
regionRule: drop a triangle when all three of its vertices are in hidden regions

stockings.desc: knitted wool stockings, knee to ankle

breeches.desc: loose knee breeches gathered below the knee

shoes.desc: low leather shoes with a tongue and a ribbon tie

boots.desc: tall soldier's boots with a turned-down cuff

doublet.desc: fitted doublet with tabbed skirt, sleeves, shirt cuffs and buttons

collar_band.desc: plain white linen falling band collar

smock.desc: loose peasant smock to mid-thigh, long sleeves

bodice.desc: laced bodice with three-quarter sleeves and chemise cuffs

kerchief.desc: white linen neckerchief / partlet over the shoulders

skirt.desc: long full wool skirt, gathered at the waist

belt.desc: leather belt with a brass buckle (sits over the smock)

coif.desc: white linen cap covering the hair, framing the face

hat_wide.desc: wide-brimmed felt hat with a low crown and a band

hat_pilgrim.desc: pilgrim's hat: low round crown, wide brim pinned up at the front, a scallop shell

cap_flat.desc: soft floppy woollen bonnet that sits on the head and droops to one side

morion.desc: Spanish cabasset helmet: tall pear-shaped bowl, narrow brim, little stalk

beguine_veil.desc: beguine headdress: white wimple closed round the face and under the chin, white veil to the shoulder blades

huik.desc: the huik: long black hooded mantle from the head to below the knees, with the tuit on top

habit.desc: long religious habit to the ankles with wide sleeves (Capuchin brown / beguine black)

rope_belt.desc: knotted cord belt with hanging ends (sits over the habit)

capuche.desc: Capuchin hood (down, long point) on a short shoulder cape

pelerine.desc: pilgrim's short shoulder cape, open at the front, with two scallop shells

buff_coat.desc: soldier's sleeveless buff-leather coat to mid-thigh, worn over the doublet

sash.desc: the Spanish army's red field sash, right shoulder to left hip, knotted

hair_long.desc: shoulder-length hair with a centre parting (1650 fashion)

hair_thin.desc: thin grey hair: bald crown, fringe round the sides and back

hair_child.desc: boy's bowl-cut hair with a straight fringe

hair_bun.desc: hair parted in the middle and swept back into a bun; soft hairline, worn bare or under a coif

beard_pointed.desc: pointed chin beard and upturned moustache (1650 fashion)

beard_full.desc: full rounded spade beard with moustache (older men)

skullcap.desc: small black skullcap (zucchetto) on the crown; wear it with hair_thin or hair_crop

bands.desc: clerical white collar with two short tabs at the throat (over the habit / cassock)

plume.desc: ostrich feather curling back from the band of the wide hat

bandolier.desc: musketeer's leather bandolier, left shoulder to right hip, with wooden powder charges

mantle.desc: the hero's travelling mantle: shoulder cape, small standing collar with a brass clasp, and a full fall down the back to the calves on the cloak chain; open in front

hair_braid.desc: hair swept back from a centre parting into one long plait down the back (lies over the mantle when one is worn)

hair_tail.desc: hair combed back and tied at the nape in a short tail with a leather thong

onderrok.desc: petticoat (onderrok): full and pleated, to the lower calf, worn under the hitched rok

rok.desc: the rok: woollen overskirt gathered at the waist and hitched up at the front corners (opgeschort) over the onderrok, falling long behind

schort.desc: the schort: a short working apron of linen over the rok, tied at the waist

jak.desc: the jak: a woman's fitted jacket, buttoned, with full sleeves, wide turned-back cuffs (accent) and a flared basque over the hips

kraag_f.desc: wide flat linen collar (platte kraag) over the shoulders, worn on the jak or the bodice

waist_sash.desc: a silk sash round the waist, knotted at the left hip with two hanging ends

boots_f.desc: a woman's soft riding boots to the calf, laced at the front, no turned-down cuff

casaque.desc: the casaque: a loose riding coat to mid-thigh over the doublet, open in front, with wide sleeves and turned-back cuffs (accent)

jerkin.desc: a sleeveless leather jerkin to the hip with a tabbed skirt, over the doublet

hair_f_curls.desc: 1640s fashion: centre parting, smooth over the crown, bunches of ringlets at both sides of the face and a small knot behind

hair_f_loose.desc: long loose hair from a centre parting, down over the back to the shoulder blades, a few strands at the temples

hair_f_twin.desc: parted in the middle, two plaits from behind the ears down the back

hair_f_crown.desc: plaits wound round the head like a crown, soft over the brow

hair_f_low.desc: soft waves drawn back into a low knot at the nape, loose strands at the temples

hair_f_fringe.desc: a short curled fringe over the brow (1640s), the rest drawn back into a bun

hair_f_tail.desc: drawn back and tied high with a ribbon (accent), a long tail down the back

hair_m_curly.desc: thick curls to the shoulders, no parting (the cavalier's mane)

hair_m_lovelock.desc: long hair with a lovelock: one longer plaited lock on the left tied with a ribbon (accent)

hair_m_shag.desc: unkempt hair to the jaw, a ragged fringe over the brow

hair_m_swept.desc: swept straight back from the brow, falling to the collar behind

hair_m_fringe.desc: short hair combed forward into a straight fringe

moustache_wide.desc: a wide moustache with upturned ends

beard_goatee.desc: a small tuft under the lower lip (mouche) and a thin moustache

beard_short.desc: a short, close full beard along the jaw, with a moustache

hat_f.desc: a woman's riding hat: tall felt crown, modest brim, a ribbon band (accent)

hat_tall.desc: a tall-crowned felt hat (the capotain) with a band and a buckle

hat_straw.desc: a wide flat straw hat with a low crown and a ribbon (accent), for the market and the road

bontmuts.desc: a woman's winter cap: a soft dyed crown with a thick roll of fur round it

muts_f.desc: a soft dark woollen bonnet worn flat on the crown over a white cap edge

cap_knit.desc: a knitted woollen cap with a rolled brim (soldiers, sailors, carters)

mantle_short.desc: the hero's short riding mantle: shoulder cape, standing collar and a fall to the hips

mantle_hood.desc: the hero's long mantle with a hood lying down on the back

eyepatch.desc: a black leather eyepatch over the right eye on a thin cord

clipNotes: one shared set keyed on rig.man; stride = metres covered per loop on the man body (1.70 m); scale the pelvis translation track by bodies[b].pelvisScale for other bodies
faceMorphNotes: morph targets of these names, in this order, on every body mesh and on the pieces marked morphs:true; drive them together with the same weights
skinToneNotes: multiply into the base colour of body meshes where COLOR_0.r = 1 (skin; 0 on lips and eyes)
